title: Settings screen: household config, category management pointer, CSV/JSON export, demo-data wipe
goal: Ship a /settings page (REQ-21) that gives the household one place to edit household config -- including the households.notify_email write path E-13's digest has been waiting on -- jump to the existing catalog manager, export their own data as CSV/JSON, and safely reset the synthetic demo household.
in_scope: New route app/settings/page.tsx (Server Component), same onboarding-gate + force-dynamic pattern as every other page (redirect to /onboarding if !household.onboarded_at). Linked from the Today page (app/page.tsx) as a new 'Settings' entry in its existing outbound-links card -- this app has no global nav (every prior UI epic has noted this), Today is the one surface every session lands on.

Household config form (name, monthly_budget, notify_email) backed by a new Server Action updateHouseholdSettingsAction in app/settings/actions.ts. Writes households via getDefaultHouseholdId() (never a client-suppliable household id). Server-side validation, not just client-side: monthly_budget rejects negative values; notify_email rejects syntactically-invalid input (a simple RFC-5322-ish regex, not a full validator library -- this app has none installed) -- both return a typed error result rather than silently accepting garbage, closing the exact 'budget field silently accepts a negative number' failure class flagged for this epic. currency and timezone are NOT exposed as editable fields -- both are hardcoded app-wide today (lib/date.ts's HOUSEHOLD_TIMEZONE comment: 'fixed to Asia/Kolkata... not read from households.timezone'); exposing an edit control for a value nothing else in the app actually reads would be a broken control, not a feature.

notify_email write path closes E-13/S-32's documented activation gap verbatim: once set, the daily/weekly digest cron routes (lib/notifications/digest.ts) stop skipping with reason 'no notify_email configured' and will attempt a real send the next time RESEND_API_KEY + RESEND_FROM_EMAIL are also configured (both remain genuinely unset in this environment -- external account setup, outside this epic's authority, unaffected by this story).

Category management / catalog manager pointer: a plain link from Settings to the existing /catalog page (app/catalog/page.tsx, shipped in an earlier epic -- merge/archive/recategorize already live there). REQ-21's 'category management' and 'catalog manager' are the same existing surface; this story makes it discoverable from Settings, it does not add a second catalog UI.

CSV/JSON export via two Server Actions in app/settings/actions.ts, each returning the file content as a string (client triggers the browser download via a Blob URL -- no new download infrastructure needed). Both scoped exclusively to getDefaultHouseholdId() -- never the demo household. JSON = a structured snapshot: household (name, currency, timezone, monthly_budget, notify_email, onboarded_at -- the household's own settings, self-directed download, not shared with a third party), catalog_items, stock_movements, price_history, and receipts metadata (merchant, purchased_at, total_amount, parse_model/tokens/cost -- storage_paths deliberately excluded, those are internal Storage keys, not user-facing data). CSV = a single flat purchase/movement ledger (one row per stock_movements row: occurred_at as a Kolkata date string, type, item name, category name, qty_base, base_unit, source receipt's merchant) -- the one genuinely tabular, spreadsheet-useful view of this domain; JSON carries the full-fidelity multi-table backup CSV structurally can't.

Demo-data wipe: a Settings button + wipeDemoDataAction Server Action calling a new lib/settings/demo-data.ts::wipeDemoHouseholdData(). Deletes item_stats_history, item_stats, price_history, stock_movements, item_aliases, catalog_items -- same table set and FK-safe order as scripts/seed-history.ts's existing wipeDemoData(), now reachable from the UI instead of only a CLI script. The household row itself is left intact (is_demo stays true, ready for re-seeding via npm run seed:history), matching the script's own upsert-not-recreate behavior.

DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID moved to lib/household.ts as a shared exported constant (single source of truth); scripts/lib/supabaseAdmin.ts updated to import it instead of redeclaring the same literal UUID a second time -- removes a drift risk between the app-side wipe action and the script-side one now that both need the value.

wipeDemoHouseholdData() hard-pins its target to the DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID constant -- the action signature takes no household-id parameter from the caller -- plus an explicit runtime assertion that DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID !== getDefaultHouseholdId() before any delete runs (belt-and-suspenders mirroring the script's own assertDemoHousehold, even though the two are fixed, distinct UUIDs today).
out_of_scope: Currency/timezone editing -- both hardcoded app-wide (lib/date.ts), not wired to households.currency/timezone anywhere else; editing them here would be a control with no effect elsewhere.
Category CRUD (create/rename/reorder categories) -- REQ-21's 'category management' is served by the existing catalog manager's merge/archive/recategorize, not a new categories-table editor.
Cost meter UI and the ingestion loop-bug guard -- S-34.
Any change to RLS policies -- still written-but-disabled per REQ-26, untouched by this story.
A confirmation-dialog UX beyond a basic browser confirm() on the demo-data wipe button -- no new modal component introduced for one destructive action on a non-production dataset.
acceptance: Data export produces valid CSV/JSON; demo-data wipe only touches is_demo-flagged rows.
invariants: updateHouseholdSettingsAction rejects a negative monthly_budget and a syntactically-invalid notify_email server-side -- never trusts client-side-only validation, never silently stores either.
wipeDemoHouseholdData() only ever deletes rows scoped to the fixed DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID constant; there is no code path by which getDefaultHouseholdId()'s household can be targeted.
CSV/JSON export queries are scoped exclusively to getDefaultHouseholdId() -- the demo household's data never appears in an export.
app/settings/page.tsx follows the same onboarding-gate + force-dynamic pattern as every other page in this app.
